rv.q: Until then, she and her human co-stars provide a late summer afternoon’s dream.

Francis O’Connor’s set design provides two levels upon which the action can take place; the aforementioned walkway also includes a cage (the Duke imprisons Sylvia, supposedly for her own good), and the lower level has several entrance/exit points.
Somewhat laboured comedy enlivened by a warm, all-male cast...
However, regrettably there was so much that was wrong with this production that it failed to spark any interest in the plot, and those 90 minutes or so felt interminably long.

cn.t: The RSC's family-friendly production receives mixed reviews, with critics praising the scene-stealing dog but questioning whether this early Shakespeare work successfully engages younger audiences despite its musical staging.
